coverage_limits: OpenAlex's anonymous daily budget ran out early in the run (list queries returned 429 and singleton lookups took about 40 seconds), so citing-works passes for the syntheses were not run; the Semantic Scholar batch endpoint and some Crossref bursts were also rate-limited. Taylor & Francis, ScienceDirect, Springer and MDPI landing pages blocked scripted access, so the abstracts of Guo 2026, Ren 2026, Chai 2026, Tian & Zheng 2025, Bal & Arseven 2026 and Fang 2025 were not read; for these and for Shi 2026 only Crossref reference lists were mined, so which references were included primary studies is inferred, not confirmed. Yao 2025's included-study list sits in an unreleased supplement (only its cited studies were extracted); Peng 2025 marks included studies only in its unstructured references; Vaccaro 2024's generative-AI creation-task rows have no creativity outcome. Several Chinese-, Indonesian- and Spanish-language studies cited in these reviews (CNKI theses, local journals without Crossref DOIs) were not verified, and for about 20 included primary records the design and sample size come from titles, review tables or search snippets rather than the abstract (each such case is flagged in its evidence field).

candidates.title: Uneven Gains of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Creativity Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of human-only vs human-generative-AI creative task performance
candidates.evidence: Pools 29 articles (44 independent studies, 141 effect sizes) that compare human-only with human-AI collaborative creative performance; overall Hedges' g = 0.54 [0.27, 0.81], larger for non-experts and general domains, with signs of publication bias. The included-study list is in supplementary materials that the authors have not released (OSF says data will be shared on publication), so primary studies were taken from its reference list.

candidates.title: Enhancing students’ Creativity with Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative-AI interventions on students' creativity
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 19 empirical studies; overall effect of generative AI on students' creativity g = 0.908, moderated by the role given to the AI, the mode of student-AI interaction and intervention duration (numbers from a search-engine snippet of the publisher abstract; the T&F page returned 403). Its 97-item Crossref reference list was mined for primary studies.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-supported instructional interventions on students’ creative thinking: a meta-analysis of 56 experimental studies
candidates.venue: Journal of Research on Technology in Education
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI-supported instruction on creative thinking
candidates.evidence: Pools 56 experimental studies with 9,643 participants; AI-supported instruction has a moderate positive effect on students' creative thinking (SMD = 0.54), moderated by stage of AI development, AI role and other factors. Most included studies use robots or non-generative AI; the generative-AI subset was extracted from its reference list.

candidates.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Nurturing Creativity: A Systematic Review of the Early Adoption Phase
candidates.authors: Lo Presti, Tosto, Rivoltella, Allegra, Gentile
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI for creativity in education (Jan 2022 to Mar 2024)
candidates.evidence: Narrative systematic review of 27 studies (20 empirical, 7 theoretical) published January 2022 to March 2024; no meta-analysis. Most empirical studies are workshops without control groups; only Lim et al. 2023 compares human and AI artifacts, and creativity of the person is the most frequent outcome (16 studies).

candidates.title: How generative artificial intelligence influences the creative thinking of STEAM learners in higher education: A systematic literature review
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI and creative thinking in higher-education STEAM
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review on generative AI and the creative thinking of STEAM learners in higher education. The abstract was not reachable (ScienceDirect blocked; no abstract in Crossref, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar), so the number of included studies is not confirmed; its 158-item reference list was mined for primary studies.

candidates.title: Effects of AI Interventions Across Cognitive, Social-emotional, and Academic Outcomes: a Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with Nonlinear Dose–response Evidence
candidates.authors: Ren, Li, Gao, Wei, Liu, Yu
candidates.task: meta-analysis of RCTs of AI interventions, creativity among cognitive outcomes
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis restricted to randomized controlled trials of AI interventions on cognitive, social-emotional and academic outcomes, with dose-response modelling. Pooled counts and the creativity estimate were not confirmed (abstract not reachable); creativity trials in its 220-item reference list are Niloy et al. 2024, Saritepeci & Yildiz Durak 2024, Urban et al. 2024, Lee & Chung 2024, Bian et al. 2025 and Li 2023.

candidates.title: When combinations of humans and AI are useful: A systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of human-AI combinations vs best of humans or AI alone
candidates.evidence: Its OSF data file holds 370 effect sizes from human-AI experiments published 2020-2023; synergy is negative for decision tasks (g = -0.27) and positive but not significant for creation tasks (g = 0.19 [-0.09, 0.48], 34 effect sizes). The only generative-AI creation tasks in the data are social-media summary post-editing (Lai et al. 2022) and code translation (Weisz et al. 2022), neither scoring creativity or diversity, so it contributes no primary creativity study.

candidates.title: Uncovering the effect of Gen AI-assisted learning on students’ creativity: A meta-analysis from quasi-experimental evidence
candidates.task: meta-analysis of quasi-experiments on generative-AI-assisted learning and creativity
candidates.evidence: New meta-analysis (not in the existing collection) of quasi-experimental studies of generative-AI-assisted learning on students' creativity. The abstract was not reachable, so the number of studies and pooled effect are not confirmed; its 84-item Crossref reference list includes Chandrasekera 2024, Essel 2024, Habib 2024, Khuibut 2023, Li 2023, Niloy 2024, Saritepeci 2024, Tang 2024, Toma 2024 and Urban 2024.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Student Creativity in Art and Design Education: A Meta-Analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI and student creativity in art and design education
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 31 experimental, quasi-experimental and correlational student studies (searches January 2020 to January 2026); overall d = 0.61 [0.49, 0.73], largest for originality/novelty outcomes and text-to-image tools. Its asterisked included list mixes experiments with perception and correlational studies; the experiments were extracted as separate records.

candidates.title: Students’ writing skills and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence: A systematic review of creativity across diverse AI-supported writing contexts
candidates.task: systematic review of creativity in AI-supported writing
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of creativity across AI-supported writing contexts; abstract not reachable, so the number of included studies is not confirmed. Its reference list includes Alzubi 2025, Niloy 2024, Pont-Niclos 2024, Woo 2023/2024 and de Vicente-Yagüe-Jara 2023.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in teaching creative writing: A systematic review in L1 and additional languages learning contexts
candidates.authors: Acosta Sánchez, Trujillo Sáez, Cantizano Márquez
candidates.task: systematic review of AI in creative-writing instruction
candidates.evidence: PRISMA review of 21 experimental or quasi-experimental studies (2019-2025) on AI in creative-writing teaching; ten have control and experimental groups (e.g., Boumous 2024, Niloy 2024, Pellas 2023, Kaşkaya & Ateş 2025, Wang et al. 2025, Zhao 2024). Reports mixed originality effects: AI broadens vocabulary and themes but can reduce originality with over-reliance.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-based painting technology on children’s creative thinking
candidates.task: systematic review of AI painting tools and children's creative thinking
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 20 empirical articles on AI-based painting tools and children's creative thinking; finds gains in creative expression but flags a risk of cognitive homogenization from standardized interfaces. Included studies cited include StoryDrawer (2022), Project Co-Art (2022), ChatScratch (2024) and Lim et al. (2023).

candidates.title: Enhancing or Hindering Mathematical Creativity? A Systematic Literature Review of Generative AI in Secondary Mathematics Education
candidates.venue: Education, Social Sciences, and Linguistics: Conference Series 2(2), 147-156
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI and mathematical creativity
candidates.evidence: PRISMA review of 27 empirical articles (2023-2026) on generative AI in secondary mathematics; finds support for fluency, flexibility and originality but also cognitive dependence and a decline in originality and idea diversity (2 articles). No DOI found on the article page.

candidates.title: Impacto de la inteligencia artificial en el desarrollo de la creatividad de los estudiantes en educación artística: Revisión Sistemática
candidates.task: systematic review of AI and creativity in arts education
candidates.evidence: PRISMA review of 19 studies (2023-2026) on AI and student creativity in arts education; reports expanded divergent thinking alongside risks of aesthetic homogenization and cultural bias.

candidates.title: Generative AI in STEAM Education: Applications and Development Prospects for Promoting Artistic Creativity
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI and artistic creativity in STEAM
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 21 empirical studies (January 2021 to January 2026, six databases) on generative AI and artistic creativity in STEAM education, coded qualitatively; no pooled estimate.

candidates.title: A Systematic Review of Artistic Human-AI Co-Creative Systems and Interaction Design
candidates.venue: ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems
other_versions: arXiv 2506.21333 (titled 'A Systematic Review of Human-AI Co-Creativity', 62 papers)
candidates.task: systematic review of artistic co-creative systems
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 63 papers on artistic human-AI co-creative systems (visual art, design, writing), deriving design dimensions and 15 design considerations; synthesizes user experience and creativity support rather than pooled creativity effects.

candidates.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on students’ 4C skills: A meta-analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI on critical thinking, creativity, communication, collaboration
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of AI effects on students' 4C skills, including creativity; abstract not reachable, so counts and the creativity estimate are not confirmed. Its reference list is dominated by robotics studies; generative-AI creativity entries are Niloy 2024 and Zhao 2024.

candidates.title: Does Generative Artificial Intelligence Improve Students’ Higher-Order Thinking? A Meta-Analysis Based on 29 Experiments and Quasi-Experiments
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI on higher-order thinking incl. creativity
candidates.evidence: Pools 29 experiments and quasi-experiments; generative AI has a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking, largest for problem solving and smallest for creativity (creativity effect about 0.444 per a search snippet of the full text).

candidates.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on students’ higher order thinking: Evidence from a three-level meta-analysis
candidates.task: three-level meta-analysis of generative AI on higher-order thinking
candidates.evidence: Three-level meta-analysis of generative AI and students' higher-order thinking; included here because its references contain creativity experiments (Niloy 2024, Saritepeci 2024, Urban 2024, Lee & Chung 2024, Doshi & Hauser 2024). Counts and any creativity sub-estimate not confirmed (abstract not reachable).

candidates.title: Generative AI-enhanced human-AI collaborative conceptual design: A systematic literature review
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI in conceptual design
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review of generative AI's influence on conceptual design and human-AI interaction, proposing a collaboration framework; the number of reviewed studies was not available from the record.

candidates.title: Integrating Generative AI in Higher Art Education: A Systematic Review of Tools, Pedagogies, and Practices
candidates.task: systematic review of generative AI in higher art education
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of generative-AI tools, pedagogies and practices in higher art education, cited by Özkan 2026; abstract not retrieved, so scope and counts are not confirmed.

candidates.title: AI-Integrated Scaffolding to Enhance Agency and Creativity in K-12 English Language Learners: A Systematic Review
candidates.task: systematic review of AI scaffolding for K-12 EFL writing creativity
candidates.evidence: Thematic synthesis of 14 empirical studies (2018-2024) on AI tools scaffolding K-12 EFL writing, focused on student agency and creativity (story generation, narrative feedback); no pooled estimate.

candidates.title: Student Creativity at Risk: A Scoping Review of the Negative Effects of Generative AI in University Education
candidates.authors: Umán Juarez, Hurtado Laura De Mera, Alcántara Cuba De Byrne, Byrne Jaramillo, Chung Sanchez
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 5th LACCEI International Multiconference on Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Regional Development (LEIRD 2025)
candidates.task: scoping review of negative effects of generative AI on student creativity
candidates.evidence: Scoping review of 26 open-access Scopus studies (2022-2025) on negative effects of AI-generated content on university students' creativity; recurring patterns are loss of divergent thinking, reduced originality and creative dependency.

candidates.title: From maker to curator: a scoping review of generative artificial intelligence in design higher education
candidates.task: scoping review of generative AI in design higher education
candidates.evidence: Scoping review of 156 studies on AI and generative AI in design higher education; creativity development is the most common focus (35.9 percent), but outcome reporting is often unspecified; no pooled estimate.

candidates.title: THE CO-CREATION BETWEEN GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND HUMAN THINKING IN EDUCATIONAL CONTEXTS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
candidates.task: systematic review of generative-AI co-creation and divergent thinking in education
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 40 studies (2020-2025) reporting moderate to large Hedges' g for divergent-thinking indicators when generative AI supports problem solving and co-creation (from the IATED abstract).

candidates.title: Nurturing Creative Learning Through Generative AI: A Systematic Review
candidates.authors: Pérez-Jorge, Pirrone, González-Herrera, Martínez-Murciano, Olmos Raya
candidates.venue: Generative AI in Education (Springer Nature Singapore), pp. 371-396
candidates.task: systematic review (book chapter) of generative AI and creative learning
candidates.evidence: Book-chapter systematic review of generative AI tools (GPT-4, GANs) and creativity in education, concluding AI enhances originality and flexibility; number of studies not given in the record.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Creativity in K–12 Education: A Systematic Scoping Review of the Literature from 2017 to 2025
candidates.task: scoping review of generative AI and creativity in K-12
candidates.evidence: Conference-paper scoping review of 45 studies (2017-2025) grouped into automated creativity scoring, human-AI co-creativity, stakeholder perceptions and creativity-enhancement interventions; no effect sizes reported.

candidates.title: Can Generative AI influence creativity? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI and student creativity
candidates.evidence: Conference meta-analysis of 12 experimental studies on generative AI and student creativity; only studies using self-report creativity tools show a significant, moderately strong effect (no numeric estimate in the summary).

candidates.title: Fostering Higher-Order Thinking with Generative AI: A Meta-Analysis (Poster 12)
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI on higher-order thinking
candidates.evidence: Poster meta-analysis of 24 experiments and quasi-experiments (2022-2025, 35 effect sizes) finding g = 0.636 for generative AI on higher-order thinking; included for recall because creativity is usually a component of higher-order thinking, though the summary does not report a creativity estimate.

candidates.title: Empowering Engineering Students Through Artificial Intelligence (AI): Blended Human–AI Creative Ideation Processes With ChatGPT
candidates.venue: Computer Applications in Engineering Education 33(1), e22817
candidates.task: engineering-student idea generation with vs without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Randomized controlled experiment with third-year engineering students (728 ideas) comparing ChatGPT-assisted with unassisted ideation; no significant differences in ideation outcomes overall, but differences by prior ChatGPT experience. Cited by Shi 2026, Yao 2025 and Guo 2026; distinct from the authors' 2026 crossover study in Thinking Skills and Creativity.

candidates.title: How Students Develop Creative Skills and Critical Thinking with ChatGPT: Experimental Results
candidates.task: weekly project writing with chatbots only vs other resources
candidates.evidence: Sixteen students in two groups prepared weekly materials, one using only AI chatbots and the control using any resource except chatbots; creative skills and critical thinking were comparatively underdeveloped in the chatbot group. Authors come from a university repository snippet (Crossref and OpenAlex list none). Cited by Shi 2026.

candidates.title: Can artificial intelligence support creativity in early design processes?
candidates.task: urban furniture design with vs without text-to-image AI
candidates.evidence: Forty design students randomly assigned to two groups; in phase 1 one group used a text-to-image tool for a design task, and in phase 2 both groups did a similar task without AI, allowing a carry-over comparison of design creativity. Cited by Shi 2026, Yao 2025 and Chai 2026.

candidates.title: How does generative artificial intelligence impact student creativity?
candidates.task: alternate uses test with and without ChatGPT-3 in a creativity course
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study in a college creativity course scoring fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality on an AUT to gauge ChatGPT-3's effect on divergent thinking; reports both support and harms to creative confidence. Included in Yao 2025, Shi 2026, Chai 2026, Özkan 2026 and Lo Presti 2026.

candidates.title: Hybrid ideas of artificial intelligence and human: Growth of creativity in college educational programs.
candidates.venue: Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts 20(4), 945-958
candidates.task: AI-human hybrid ideation in college programs
candidates.evidence: Study of creativity growth from hybrid AI-human ideas in college programs, included in Shi 2026's meta-analysis; the abstract was not retrievable, so design and sample are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Exploring the effect of ChatGPT-3 on biology students' lateral thinking skills: a mixed-methods study and impacts for ai-enhanced education
candidates.task: listing innovative biological energy sources without, then with, ChatGPT-3
candidates.evidence: 110 undergraduates did a Guilford-type ideation task (fluency, flexibility, elaboration, originality) alone and, four weeks later, with ChatGPT-3; within-subject comparison of lateral-thinking scores. Cited by Shi 2026.

candidates.title: ChatGPT-Related Risk Patterns and Students’ Creative Thinking Toward Tourism Statistics Course: Pretest and Posttest Quasi-Experimentation
candidates.task: tourism statistics course with ChatGPT use
candidates.evidence: Survey of 1,443 students (PLS-SEM) plus a pre/post quasi-experiment linking ChatGPT use and its perceived risks to students' creative thinking; creativity may be partly self-reported. Cited by Shi 2026.

candidates.title: Can Generative Artificial Intelligence be a Good Teaching Assistant?—An Empirical Analysis Based on Generative AI-Assisted Teaching
candidates.venue: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 41(3), e70027
candidates.task: classroom teaching: computer-assisted vs generative AI with/without teacher supervision
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment comparing traditional computer-assisted teaching with generative-AI-assisted teaching with and without teacher supervision over two weeks; included in Shi 2026's creativity meta-analysis, but the abstract snippet does not confirm a creativity outcome.

candidates.title: Effects of ChatGPT use on undergraduate students’ creativity: a threat to creative thinking?
candidates.task: 10 weeks of ChatGPT-assisted assignments; CREA creativity test before and after
candidates.evidence: One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT for 10 weeks of assignments and took the CREA creative-intelligence test (unassisted) before and after; no evidence of decline (25 percent decreased, 54 percent improved). Cited by Shi, Yao, Chai and Aisiya.

candidates.title: EEG assessment of artificial intelligence-generated content impact on student creative performance and neurophysiological states in product design
candidates.task: three-hour walking-cane design task with AIGC tools vs traditional software
candidates.evidence: 64 third-year design students in two groups (ChatGPT, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion vs traditional design software); creative performance rated with standardized design criteria plus EEG; the abstract (truncated in the record) reports a significant enhancement with AIGC tools. Cited by Shi 2026.

candidates.title: Integration of AI GPTs in music education and their impact on students’ perception and creativity
candidates.task: music education with GPT tools
candidates.evidence: Study of GPT integration in music education and its impact on students' creativity, included in Shi 2026's meta-analysis; abstract not retrievable, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI on collaborative problem-solving and team creativity performance in digital story creation: an experimental study
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education 22, 23
candidates.task: 20-week digital storytelling with ChatGPT, Midjourney and Runway vs traditional methods
candidates.evidence: Sixty university students randomly assigned to create digital stories with generative-AI tools or by traditional methods; outcomes are collaborative problem solving and team creativity performance (pre/post surveys and interviews). Cited by Shi 2026 and Guo 2026.

candidates.title: The Role and Evaluation of ChatGPT as a Virtual Tutor in Improving Students' Creative and Critical Abilities Reviewed from Probing-Prompting Abilities
candidates.task: high-school mathematics with ChatGPT as virtual tutor
candidates.evidence: Embedded mixed-methods study of 20 grade-12 students using ChatGPT as a math tutor, measuring gains in mathematical, creative and critical abilities by written tests; single group, no control. Cited by Shi 2026 and Aisiya 2026.

candidates.title: Do AI-generative tools kill or nurture creativity in EFL teaching and learning?
candidates.task: EFL writing with generative AI tools
candidates.evidence: Study of whether generative AI tools help or hurt creativity in EFL teaching and learning, cited by Peng 2025, Zhao 2025 and Bal & Arseven 2026; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: ChatGPT effects on cognitive skills of undergraduate students: Receiving instant responses from AI-based conversational large language models (LLMs)
candidates.task: flipped research-methods course using ChatGPT vs databases and search engines
candidates.evidence: 125 Ghanaian students randomly allocated to use ChatGPT (60) or traditional databases and search engines (65) for in-class tasks; pretest-posttest Creative Thinking Scale alongside critical and reflective thinking (creativity measured by a scale, possibly self-report). Cited by Peng 2025 and Chai 2026.

candidates.title: Supermind Ideator: How Scaffolding Human-AI Collaboration Can Increase Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI '24), pp. 18-28
candidates.task: creative problem solving with an LLM-based ideation scaffold
candidates.evidence: Experimental study in which people using Supermind Ideator (an LLM with prompts, fine-tuning and a scaffolded interface) generated significantly more creative solutions than comparison users; assignment and N not stated in the retrieved abstract. Cited by Peng 2025.

candidates.title: Does human–AI collaboration lead to more creative art? Aesthetic evaluation of human-made and AI-generated haiku poetry
candidates.task: haiku: human-only vs AI-only vs human-in-the-loop AI
candidates.evidence: 385 raters evaluated haiku written by professional poets, generated by AI alone, or generated by AI with human selection (human-in-the-loop); human-in-the-loop haiku were rated most highly while AI-only and human-only scored similarly (bibliographic data from Crossref; design details from university news summaries). Cited by Peng 2025.

candidates.title: Comparing AIGC and traditional idea generation methods: Evaluating their impact on creativity in the product design ideation phase
candidates.authors: Lin, Jiang, Deng, Bian, Fang, Zhu
candidates.task: product design ideation with AIGC vs traditional methods
candidates.evidence: Compares AIGC-based and traditional idea generation methods on creativity in product design ideation; included in Peng 2025 and Özkan 2026, but the abstract was not retrievable, so design and N are unconfirmed. Distinct from the collected Lin (2026) divergent-thinking study.

candidates.title: Collaborative AI-enhanced digital mind-mapping as a tool for stimulating creative thinking in inclusive education for students with neurodevelopmental disorders
candidates.task: collaborative digital mind-mapping with AI prompts in inclusive groups
candidates.evidence: 163 students (28 with neurodevelopmental disorders) used collaborative digital mind-mapping with AI-provided prompts; Torrance Figural fluency, originality, elaboration and total creativity rose significantly pre to post (Wilcoxon). Cited by Yao 2025 and Guo 2026.

candidates.title: How and for whom using generative AI affects creativity: A field experiment.
candidates.task: employees at a technology consulting firm with vs without LLM assistance
candidates.evidence: Field experiment randomly assigning employees of a technology consulting firm to LLM (ChatGPT) assistance or not; supervisor and external-evaluator creativity ratings rose with LLM use, especially for employees high in metacognitive strategies. N = 250 comes from university news coverage, not the abstract. Cited by Yao 2025, Zhao 2025 and Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: Enhanced creativity at the cost of increased stress? The impact of generative AI on serious games for creativity stimulation
candidates.task: serious games for creativity stimulation with vs without generative AI
candidates.evidence: Examines how adding generative AI to creativity-stimulation serious games affects creative output and stress, cited by Yao 2025; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: StoryDrawer: A Child–AI Collaborative Drawing System to Support Children's Creative Visual Storytelling
candidates.venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '22), pp. 1-15
candidates.task: children's visual storytelling with AI drawing strategies
candidates.evidence: 2x2 study with 64 children aged 6-10 varying two AI strategies (real-time drawing of the child's telling; generated abstract sketches); the system provoked more creative and elaborate ideas and outcomes. Cited by Lo Presti 2026 and the Wang et al. 2025 painting review.

candidates.title: Exploring cognitive strategies in human-AI interaction: ChatGPT's role in creative tasks
candidates.task: creative tasks with ChatGPT; cognitive strategies
candidates.evidence: Study of cognitive strategies when people use ChatGPT on creative tasks, cited by Guo 2026; abstract not retrieved, so whether creativity is compared with a no-AI condition is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: An Innovative Solution to Design Problems: Applying the Chain-of-Thought Technique to Integrate LLM-Based Agents With Concept Generation Methods
candidates.task: concept generation (brainstorming, TRIZ) with GPT-4 agents vs human partners
candidates.evidence: Thirty participants in two phases compared human-agent with human-human collaboration under brainstorming and TRIZ, measuring creative thinking performance and electrodermal activity; LLM agents reduced cognitive load while creativity was maintained. Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Student-AI collaborative creative Problem-Solving: The role of human agency
candidates.task: student-AI creative problem solving varying human agency
candidates.evidence: Study of human agency in student-AI creative problem solving, cited by Guo 2026; abstract not retrieved (a search snippet suggests generating own ideas at each AI interaction preserved independent thinking and improved creativity), so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: From metacognitive monitoring to control: How human-AI collaboration influences emergent creativity in higher education
candidates.task: 100-minute campus poster design with Doubao vs no devices
candidates.evidence: Per its public dataset, 76 undergraduates were split between a group using the Doubao assistant and a no-device control for a poster design task, with blind ratings of effectiveness, correctness and novelty plus metacognition and emotion measures; the dataset-article link is inferred from matching authors and topic. Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Collaborative Ideation: Educational Insight From Fashion Students
candidates.task: fashion design ideation workshops with image-generating AI
candidates.evidence: Design workshops and interviews with 10 fashion students ideating with image-generating AI; experts rated the AI-assisted ideas higher in originality and novelty than a control group. Cited by Guo 2026 and Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: Creative combinational design through generative AI in different dimensional representations: An exploration
candidates.authors: Wang, Han, Zhao, Yin, Chen, Childs
candidates.task: combinational design with generative AI in 2D/3D representations
candidates.evidence: Exploration of generative AI for creative combinational design across representations, cited by Guo 2026; abstract not retrieved, so whether people's creativity is compared across conditions is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Interaction between students and artificial intelligence in the context of creative potential development
candidates.task: fine arts, literary writing and fashion design students using ChatGPT-4 for ideas
candidates.evidence: Students in three creative majors were split equally into ChatGPT-4 intervention and standard-program control groups; creative thinking measured with the Torrance Figural test before and after (an unassisted test after AI use). Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on higher-order thinking skills and artificial intelligence literacy in nursing undergraduates: A quasi-experimental study
candidates.task: nursing course with generative-AI interactive teaching
candidates.evidence: 132 nursing undergraduates randomly divided into a generative-AI interactive-teaching group and a control group; outcomes are higher-order thinking skills and AI literacy. Included for recall: whether creativity is a scored component of the HOTS measure is not confirmed. Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Facilitator or hindrance? The impact of AI on university students' higher-order thinking skills in complex problem solving
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education 22, 39
candidates.task: design-problem solving with and without ChatGPT-4o (within-subject)
candidates.evidence: Within-subject experiment with 40 students on design problem modules; consensual assessment shows ChatGPT-4o slightly raised the originality and usefulness of design sketches and increased higher-order-thinking diversity. Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of artificial intelligence integration in design-based learning on design thinking mindset, creative and reflective thinking skills: An experimental study
candidates.task: digital story development with ChatGPT and Midjourney in design-based learning
candidates.evidence: Experimental study in which participants used ChatGPT and Midjourney within design-based learning vs a comparison condition; outcomes are design-thinking mindset, creative self-efficacy and reflective thinking (creativity outcome is self-efficacy, i.e., self-report). Cited by Chai 2026, Ren 2026, Nie 2025, Guo 2026 and Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: Promoting students’ creative and design thinking with generative AI-supported co-regulated learning: Evidence from digital game development projects in healthcare courses
candidates.task: digital game development projects with generative-AI co-regulated learning
candidates.evidence: 46 students in two classes: generative-AI co-regulated learning vs conventional co-regulated learning; the AI approach improved project design performance and creative thinking. Shi 2026 cites this DOI in truncated form. Metadata from DOAJ (ET&S DOIs are not in Crossref).

candidates.title: Effects of AI-generated drawing on students’ learning achievement and creativity in an ancient poetry course
candidates.task: ancient poetry learning by generating AI drawings of poem scenes
candidates.evidence: Generative-AI drawing approach in an ancient poetry course compared with a conventional approach on learning achievement and creativity (design from the DOAJ abstract; group allocation and N not captured). Cited by Shi 2026.

candidates.title: The Effects of Design-Thinking-Based AI Education Programs Utilizing Generative AI on Korean Middle School Students’ Creative Problem-Solving Ability
candidates.venue: JOIV: International Journal on Informatics Visualization 9(4), 1553
candidates.task: design-thinking AI program; generative AI for personas and storytelling
candidates.evidence: 117 middle-school students (57 experimental using generative AI in the Empathize stage, 60 control without); creative problem-solving ability (tested pre and post) improved only in the experimental group. Cited by Aisiya 2026.

candidates.title: IMPLEMENTASI PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA BERBANTUAN GEMINI.AI TERHADAP PENINGKATAN KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KREATIF DAN ADVERSITY QUOTIENT SISWA
candidates.task: grade-10 mathematics with Gemini assistance vs without
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 70 grade-10 students (35 Gemini-assisted, 35 control); creative-thinking test gains were larger with Gemini (N-gain 61.65 vs 50.42 percent per Aisiya 2026). Crossref lists only the given names Avita and Siti; family names follow Aisiya 2026's citation.

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students’ mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study
candidates.task: mathematical creativity task with vs without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment comparing college students who used ChatGPT on a mathematical creativity task with a control group that did not; ChatGPT improved mathematical creativity, self-efficacy and interest. Cited by Aisiya 2026 (which lists a slightly different author string); distinct from the collected Liu (2025) helper-comparison study.

candidates.title: Effects of Generative AI-Assisted Instruction on Creativity and Multidimensional Design Skills in Advertising Design Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study
candidates.venue: Journal of Buddhist Education and Research (JBER) 12(S1), 948-996
candidates.task: advertising design course with generative-AI-assisted vs traditional instruction
candidates.evidence: Pre/post quasi-experiment with 85 digital-media students in intact classes; generative-AI-assisted instruction outperformed traditional instruction on five design dimensions, with creativity showing the largest effect (ANCOVA). Found while searching for syntheses.

candidates.title: A Study on the Role of Midjourney, A Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool, in Enhancing Student Creativity in Illustration Design Classes
candidates.venue: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 42(5), e70305
candidates.task: illustration design studio: Midjourney workflow vs non-generative workflow
candidates.evidence: Two-section quasi-experiment (n = 162: 82 Midjourney workflow, 80 manual brainstorming and sketching); final product creativity, originality, appropriateness and elaboration were higher with Midjourney after baseline adjustment; the study logs ideation breadth and names controlling homogenisation as an aim.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.task: short story writing with GPT-5-mini vs alone, originality vs quality incentives
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered 2x2 RCT (n = 200, Prolific, block randomization) crossing AI access (GPT-5-mini vs writing alone) with originality vs technical-quality bonuses; AI-assisted stories were more similar to each other, but originality incentives restored collective diversity because participants adopted fewer AI suggestions verbatim. Found while searching for homogenization syntheses.

candidates.title: The Role of Generative AI in Human Creative Processes: Experimental Evidence
candidates.task: novel creative tasks with vs without ChatGPT access
candidates.evidence: Preregistered lab experiment: 124 university students, a random half given ChatGPT access; access worsened creative performance for those above median creative potential, and post-task creativity-potential performance was also measured. Cited by Yao 2025 and Özkan 2026; possibly an earlier version of the collected Zhu & Zou (2026, JEBO) paper, but the titles differ and identity was not confirmed.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co‐Creation
candidates.task: two AUTs, consequences task and problem solving in dyads, with internet or with AI
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in four conditions (human-human dyads, human-internet, two human-AI groups); human-human dyads scored highest on divergent thinking, with no group differences in problem solving; also compares human ratings with automated scoring. Cited by Yao 2025 and Chai 2026.

candidates.title: Is Chatgpt a menace for creative writing ability? An experiment
candidates.task: university creative-writing essays with vs without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: 600 students from 10 universities in control and experimental groups, the latter using ChatGPT in creative writing; originality, content presentation, accuracy and elaboration were scored, with detrimental effects for the ChatGPT group. Cited by Yao, Ren, Chai, Nie, Tian & Zheng, Bal & Arseven and Acosta Sánchez.

candidates.title: Integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching: An empirical study on self-efficacy and learning outcomes
candidates.task: product design ideation teaching with AIGC
candidates.evidence: Empirical study of AIGC in product design ideation teaching, with self-efficacy and learning outcomes; cited among Yao 2025's included-study references, but the abstract was not retrieved, so design and creativity measures are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Effects of a ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach on learners’ courseware project performances and perceptions
candidates.task: courseware project in a flipped class with a ChatGPT guiding approach
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with two classes (one randomly assigned to the experimental group) in which only the experimental class learned with the ChatGPT-based guiding approach; it improved project performance and creative thinking among other outcomes. Cited by Peng, Ren and Chai.

candidates.title: Integrating ChatGPT into Synectics Model to Improve High School Student's Creative Writing Skill
candidates.venue: ICCE 2023: The 31st International Conference on Computers in Education
candidates.task: high-school creative writing with ChatGPT in a synectics model
candidates.evidence: 34 high-school students in an experimental group (synectics plus ChatGPT) and 30 in a control group; the experimental group showed meaningful gains in creative writing performance. Included in Peng 2025 and cited by Chai 2026.

candidates.title: Human Creativity Vs. Artificial Intelligence: A Comparison of Horror Fiction Crafting from ‘Bookish Minds Club’ at Souk Ahras University and Claude AI
candidates.venue: Rupkatha Journal on Interdisciplinary Studies in Humanities 16(3)
candidates.task: horror short stories written alone vs with Claude AI
candidates.evidence: Sixty reading-club members split evenly into writers working alone or with Claude AI on identical horror prompts; stories rated for originality, coherence, horror effectiveness, character development and impact, with a slight advantage for unassisted writers. Included in Acosta Sánchez 2026.

candidates.title: The Effects of Generative AI Platforms on Undergraduates’ Narrative Intelligence and Writing Self-Efficacy
candidates.task: digital story creation on generative AI platforms vs conventional platforms
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest comparison of 64 undergraduates using generative AI story platforms (Sudowrite, Jasper, Shortly AI) or conventional platforms (Storybird, Storyjumper, ZooBurst); outcomes are narrative intelligence and writing self-efficacy, not a creativity score as such. Included in Acosta Sánchez 2026.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Chinese Poetry Instruction
candidates.venue: International Journal of Online Pedagogy and Course Design 15(1), 1-21
candidates.task: poetry writing with text-to-image and image-to-poetry AI
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study with pre-, mid- and post-tests of students' poetry writing ability and creative expression when using AI-generated visuals; no control group is described. Included in Acosta Sánchez 2026.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-enhanced natural language processing tools on writing proficiency: an analysis of language precision, content summarization, and creative writing facilitation
candidates.task: writing with AI NLP tools including creative writing facilitation
candidates.evidence: Study of AI-enhanced NLP tools on writing, including creative writing; Acosta Sánchez 2026 lists it among studies with control and experimental groups (students using AI more easily inspired). Abstract not retrieved; design and N unconfirmed. Also cited by Tian & Zheng 2025.

candidates.title: Enhancing Creative Writing Skills in Secondary School Students through Prompt Engineering and Artificial Intelligence
candidates.task: three-phase AI-enhanced storytelling intervention in secondary school
candidates.evidence: Intervention with 129 secondary students (descriptive writing, collaborative scriptwriting, AI-enhanced storytelling) reporting measurable gains in descriptive and imaginative writing; no control group described. Included in Acosta Sánchez 2026.

candidates.title: Writing creative stories with AI: learning designs for secondary school students
candidates.venue: Innovation in Language Learning and Teaching
candidates.task: secondary-school creative story writing with AI
candidates.evidence: Learning-design study of secondary students writing creative stories with AI; per Acosta Sánchez 2026, AI support affected elaboration most and flexibility least, without a control group. Abstract not retrieved.

candidates.title: La colaboración humano-IA como estrategia metodológica para el desarrollo de la creatividad en la educación cultural y artística
candidates.task: secondary art creation with generative AI tools
candidates.evidence: Mixed exploratory design with 60 secondary students integrating generative AI into art making; Consensual Assessment Technique ratings showed significant gains in originality, technical feasibility and conceptual depth (comparison structure not stated). Included in Drullard Alcántara 2026.

candidates.title: Gudeg Meets AI: A culturally integrated discovery learning e-book to evolute creative thinking and physics identity
candidates.venue: Journal of Technology and Science Education 15(3), 760
candidates.task: AI-assisted discovery-learning physics e-book
candidates.evidence: Research-and-development study of an AI-assisted discovery-learning e-book tested with 58 grade-12 students; creative thinking rose on pretest-posttest one-sample tests. Included for recall only: the role of generative AI for students is unclear and there is no control group. Cited by Aisiya 2026.

candidates.title: A Hybrid Prototype Method Combining Physical Models and Generative Artificial Intelligence to Support Creativity in Conceptual Design
candidates.authors: Zhang, Chen, Xie, Jiang, Zhou, Sun
candidates.task: conceptual design with physical prototypes, generative AI, or a hybrid
candidates.evidence: Comparative user study with 45 designers completing a design task with physical prototyping, standalone generative AI and a hybrid physical-plus-generative-AI method; the hybrid method best supported creativity. Cited by Yao 2025.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI model type and visual stimuli type on design creativity
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation with text-to-image vs other AI tools and visual stimuli
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment in design education varying generative-AI model type and visual stimulus type; text-to-image tools and abstract visuals raised design creativity in divergent and convergent phases, with design-fixation risk. Cited by Guo 2026 and Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: A novel idea generation tool using a structured conversational AI (CAI) system
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e11
candidates.task: novice product designers generating ideas with an LLM interface vs traditional methods
candidates.evidence: 30 novice designers generated ideas with traditional methods and with an LLM-based conversational ideation interface; experts rated fluency, novelty and variety higher for the AI interface. Found via search for design syntheses.

candidates.title: Generative AI: A double-edged sword for creative thinking learning — Evidence from facial expressions and fNIRS
candidates.task: brainstorming and TRIZ creative tasks with generative AI vs traditional methods
candidates.evidence: Two groups (generative AI vs traditional methods) completed brainstorming and TRIZ tasks with facial-expression and fNIRS recording; generative AI significantly enhanced creative thinking performance but raised fear during AI-supported brainstorming (summary from the university research portal).

candidates.title: Project Co-Art: Improving Children’s Imagination Through AI-based Human-Computer Co-creation
candidates.authors: Shen, Piao, Tan, Lin, Zhao, Wan
candidates.task: children's drawing after AI visualizes their spoken sentences
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiment: children trained with Co-Art (the system draws an abstract image from the child's sentence to inspire a second drawing) produced drawings with significantly richer aesthetics and higher imagination and creativity than a non-trained group. Cited by Lo Presti 2026 and the Wang et al. 2025 painting review.

candidates.title: Enhancing art creation through AI-based generative adversarial networks in educational auxiliary system
candidates.task: undergraduate art creation with a GAN-based co-creation system
candidates.evidence: System evaluated with 60 undergraduate art students; expert-rated creative output quality rose 35.4 percent and engagement 42.7 percent relative to a comparison (comparison condition not detailed in the abstract). Cited by Guo 2026.

candidates.title: Enhancing student creative and critical thinking in generative AI-empowered creation: a mind-mapping approach
candidates.task: art-course digital storytelling with mind mapping plus generative AI vs comparison
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 45 university students in an introductory art course; the experimental group used an integrated mind-mapping and generative-AI digital-storytelling approach, with creative and critical thinking as outcomes (comparison condition truncated in abstract). Included in Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: An Empirical Study on Enhancing Artistic Creativity of College Fine Arts Students Through Generative AI-Based Creative Thinking Training
candidates.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (HCI International 2025 Late Breaking Papers), pp. 33-43
candidates.task: generative-AI creative thinking training for fine arts students
candidates.evidence: Empirical study of generative-AI-based creative-thinking training and artistic creativity, included in Özkan 2026's meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Application of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Design Education: An Exploration and Analysis to Enhance Student Creativity
candidates.task: design education with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Study of generative AI in design education to enhance creativity, included in Özkan 2026's meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Analysis of the application of generative artificial intelligence in interior design education
candidates.task: interior design education with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Analysis of generative AI in interior design education, included in Özkan 2026's creativity meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: An exploration of the role of generative AI in fostering creativity in architectural learning environments
candidates.task: architectural design studio with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study of generative AI and creativity in architectural learning environments, included in Özkan 2026's meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Using AI to Generate Visual Art: Do Individual Differences in Creativity Predict AI-Assisted Art Quality?
candidates.task: participants' word sets turned into DALL-E images, rated for creativity
candidates.evidence: Pre-registered correlational study: participants' divergent thinking (AUT, DAT) and the semantic diversity of word sets they wrote for DALL-E predicted raters' creativity scores of the resulting AI-assisted images; no no-AI condition. Included in Özkan 2026.

candidates.title: GPT-3-Driven Pedagogical Agents to Train Children’s Curious Question-Asking Skills
candidates.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education 34(2), 483-518
candidates.task: children's divergent (curious) question-asking training with GPT-3-generated cues
candidates.evidence: Compares GPT-3-generated with hand-crafted cues in training children to ask divergent questions; included for recall because divergent question generation is a creativity-adjacent outcome and Chai 2026 cites it. Design and N not captured from the abstract.

candidates.title: Supporting Teachers’ Professional Development With Generative AI: The Effects on Higher Order Thinking and Self-Efficacy
candidates.task: preservice teachers' teaching-skills training with generative AI vs traditional
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest quasi-experiment with 215 preservice teachers (generative-AI training vs traditional training) on higher-order thinking and self-efficacy; included for recall because Chai 2026's creativity meta-analysis cites it, though a creativity component is not confirmed.

candidates.title: Exploring the Application and Influence of Artificial Intelligence AIGC Technology on Logo Design
candidates.venue: Atlantis Highlights in Intelligent Systems (ICIDIT 2023), pp. 451-459
candidates.task: logo design with AIGC
candidates.evidence: Marked with an asterisk (included study) in Peng 2025's creative-thinking meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so the comparison and creativity measure are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Empirical study on the double-edged effects of generative artificial intelligence on team creativity among university students
candidates.task: university student teams and generative AI use
candidates.evidence: Empirical study of generative AI's double-edged effects on student team creativity, cited by Zhao 2025's meta-analysis; abstract not retrieved, so design (possibly a survey) is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: An Exploratory Study on Fashion Design Ideation Experiences and Creativity Using Generative AI-Based Visual Stimuli
candidates.venue: Journal of the Korean Society of Costume 76(3), 133-157
candidates.task: fashion design ideation with generative-AI visual stimuli
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study of ideation experience and creativity when fashion designers use generative-AI visual stimuli (found by title search while verifying Ge & Hou 2025); abstract not retrieved, so design and N are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: The effect of artificial intelligence-supported visualization applications on students writing disposition in the creative writing process
candidates.task: creative writing with AI image-generation visualization (DALL-E, Canva)
candidates.evidence: Control-vs-experimental study of AI image visualization in creative writing; main outcome is writing disposition (an attitude scale), though Acosta Sánchez 2026 reports better idea generation and development. Included for recall; the creativity outcome may be self-reported.

candidates.title: Impact of Generative AI Integration on Design Sketching Pedagogy in Higher Education: An Empirical Study in Mianyang, China
candidates.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Progressive Education and Development 15(2)
candidates.task: design sketching course with generative AI
candidates.evidence: Empirical study of generative AI in design-sketching teaching (found by title search); abstract not retrieved, so whether creativity is scored against a comparison is unconfirmed. Crossref author names are listed in Chinese order as given.

candidates.title: Dancing with the Unexpected and Beyond: The Use of AI Assistance in Design Fiction Creation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Tenth International Symposium of Chinese CHI, pp. 129-140
candidates.task: design-fiction writing workshop with an AI text agent
candidates.evidence: Workshop with 20 Chinese youth writing design fiction with AI-generated text; fiction quality, experiences and incorporation of AI text were analyzed, with AI raising richness and creativity; no control group described. Cited by Peng 2025.

candidates.title: ChatScratch: An AI-Augmented System Toward Autonomous Visual Programming Learning for Children Aged 6-12
candidates.authors: Chen, Xiao, Chen, Song, Wu, Sun
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), pp. 1-19
candidates.task: children's Scratch projects with storyboards, image generation and an LLM vs Scratch
candidates.evidence: Compares ChatScratch (storyboards, image generation, Scratch-specialized LLM) with plain Scratch for children aged 6-12, targeting artist's block and bounded creativity; included for recall because Peng 2025 and the Wang et al. 2025 painting review cite it, though a scored creativity outcome is not confirmed.
